patch_description: The best-known ratio-optimal 14-point arrangement in 3D has D6 symmetry: two staggered hexagonal rings (radius r, heights ±h, relative twist π/6) plus two poles (0,0,±p). For this configuration all pairwise distances have closed forms, so I first run an exact dense grid/local search over the three parameters (p, h, r) maximizing dmin/dmax directly. This gives a seed essentially at the true optimum (squared ratio target 1/4.165849767 ≈ 0.2400). I then run the existing soft-min/soft-max projected gradient polish on this seed (and a few jittered variants, plus the icosahedron fallback) to squeeze out any residual improvement, keeping the best configuration found. This replaces the previously geometrically-mismatched starting points, letting the local optimizer polish straight to the symmetric optimum instead of trying to discover it.
